entries.next_step: How might your understanding of God’s blessing need to become deeper or wider?
entries.closing: The greatest blessing of walking with God is that we walk with God.

entries.title: A Cry from the Depths
entries.greeting: Welcome. Desperation does not disqualify our prayers; it can become the place from which we call to God.
entries.consider_this:
The psalmist does not speak from a place of calm control. He cries from the depths and asks the Lord to listen. Scripture gives us language for prayer when polished words are impossible.

Fear and grief can fill our thoughts with painful memories and imagined outcomes. Telling ourselves simply to stop thinking about the problem may increase shame when the mind remains overwhelmed. God does not ask us to deny what is happening. He invites us to bring it into His Presence.

Prayer, worship, Scripture, and fasting can help turn our attention toward Jesus, but they are not techniques for forcing distress to disappear. God may also care for us through trusted friends, pastors, counsellors, doctors, medication, rest, and practical protection.

Faith from the depths may be no more than an honest cry: “Lord, have mercy.” That prayer is enough to begin. The God who hears does not despise our weakness.
entries.prayer: Lord, hear my voice from the depths. Hold what feels too heavy, quiet the shame surrounding my struggle, and lead me toward the spiritual and practical care I need. Amen.
entries.next_step: What honest cry needs to be brought into God’s Presence today?
entries.closing: Even from the depths, your voice can reach the Heart of God.

entries.title: Where Forgiveness Lets Us Stand
entries.greeting: Welcome. God knows the truth about our sin, yet in Him there is forgiveness.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 130 asks a sobering question: if God kept a record of sins, who could stand? None of us is rescued by a carefully balanced account of good actions outweighing the bad.

The Gospel gives a better Hope. Jesus carried our sin at the Cross and rose again, opening the way for forgiveness and reconciliation with God. Grace is not earned through improvement, religious effort, or self-punishment. It is received through trust in Christ.

Forgiveness does not call sin harmless. Repentance may include confession, changed behaviour, accountability, and repairing what can be repaired. Yet these actions flow from Grace; they do not purchase it.

Guilt can alert us to what needs to change. Shame tells us that we are beyond mercy. The Gospel refuses that verdict. In Jesus, we can face the truth without being destroyed by it, because the One who judges sin has also provided our Salvation.
entries.prayer: Merciful God, thank You for the forgiveness given through Jesus. Lead me into honest repentance, free me from condemning shame, and teach me to live gratefully within Your Grace. Amen.
entries.next_step: Where do you need to receive forgiveness rather than continue punishing yourself?
entries.closing: We stand before God not because our record is clean, but because Jesus has carried our sin.

entries.title: Steadfast Love, Enduring Hope
entries.greeting: Welcome. God’s Love is neither reckless nor irrational; it is holy, purposeful, and steadfast.
entries.consider_this:
Human love can become impulsive, possessive, or confused. God’s Love is different. It is not blind to our sin, and it does not abandon truth in order to remain affectionate.

The Cross reveals a Love that sees clearly and gives sacrificially. God did not save us because sin did not matter. Jesus entered our brokenness, bore its cost, and opened the way home. His Love is undeserved, but it is never meaningless or careless.

This is why the psalmist calls God’s People to Hope in the Lord. Our confidence rests in His faithful Character, not in our ability to remain impressive. He corrects because He loves, forgives because He is merciful, and remains committed to completing His Work within His People.

We may struggle to feel loved, especially when human relationships have wounded us. God’s Love is not measured by emotion alone. It is anchored in what He has done through Jesus and made present through the Holy Spirit.
entries.prayer: God of steadfast Love, root my Hope in the Cross of Jesus. Heal the distorted pictures of love I carry, and help me receive Your holy, truthful, and faithful Love. Amen.
entries.next_step: Which part of God’s steadfast Love is difficult for your heart to receive?
entries.closing: God’s Love is not careless with the truth; it is faithful enough to save and transform us.

entries.title: Quieted in God’s Hands
entries.greeting: Welcome. Peace can grow when we release what was never ours to control.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 131 pictures a quieted soul resting like a child with a trusted parent. This is not denial of danger. It is the settled recognition that we are not God and do not have to understand or manage everything.

Letting go does not mean becoming passive. We still make wise decisions, seek help, protect those in our care, and act faithfully. We release the illusion that perfect vigilance can guarantee a painless future.

Anxiety is not proof that we have failed to trust. The nervous system can remain alert even while the heart is reaching toward God. Peace may arrive gradually, alongside counselling, medical care, boundaries, rest, prayer, and the support of others.

Our confidence is not that everything will happen as we wish. It is that we are held within God’s Hands and accompanied by His Presence. The One who holds us is patient with our trembling.
entries.prayer: Father, quiet my soul within Your Hands. Give me wisdom for what is mine to do and freedom to release what belongs to You. Meet my anxiety with patience and lead me toward peace. Amen.
entries.next_step: What are you carrying as though its outcome depends entirely upon you?
entries.closing: Peace begins not in controlling everything, but in being held by the One who is faithful.

entries.title: The Beauty of Life Together
entries.greeting: Welcome. Unity is a Gift to receive and a calling to practise with truth and love.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 133 celebrates the beauty of God’s People living together in unity. Christian unity is more than avoiding disagreement. It is shared life centred upon Jesus, shaped by humility, patience, truth, repentance, and forgiveness.

Peace does not require us to tolerate abuse, conceal wrongdoing, or remain in unsafe relationships. Boundaries can be necessary and godly. At times, truth will create discomfort before genuine reconciliation becomes possible.

Yet we should also resist the habits that make community needlessly fragile: gossip, contempt, suspicion, stubborn pride, and the urge to discard people whenever relationships become difficult. The Holy Spirit teaches us to listen, speak honestly, forgive wisely, and pursue peace wherever possible.

Unity is not sameness. The Church contains different stories, personalities, cultures, and gifts. When these are gathered beneath the Lordship of Jesus, our differences can become part of the beauty of His Body.
entries.prayer: Lord Jesus, make me a faithful member of Your Body. Show me where I need humility, courage, forgiveness, or healthy boundaries, and teach me to pursue unity without abandoning truth. Amen.
entries.next_step: What might faithful peacemaking look like in a relationship that matters to you?
entries.closing: Christian unity grows where truth and love are practised beneath the Lordship of Jesus.

entries.title: Greater Than What Stands Before Us
entries.greeting: Welcome. Our problems may be greater than our strength, but they are never greater than God.
entries.consider_this:
Some challenges are genuinely enormous. Illness, grief, addiction, injustice, debt, and broken relationships cannot be reduced to a positive attitude. Faith does not ask us to pretend that these things are small.

Psalm 135 redirects our vision toward the greatness of God. He is not merely a larger version of us. He is Creator, Lord, and Redeemer. Nothing lies beyond His knowledge or Authority.

Focusing upon Jesus does not make us incapable of sadness or defeat. Faithful people can feel downcast and still belong securely to God. Looking to Him means allowing His Character and His Promises to become more decisive than fear’s claim that there is no Hope.

God may change the circumstance, or He may give strength, wisdom, community, and endurance within it. Either way, His greatness is not measured by how quickly our problems disappear. It is revealed supremely in Jesus, whose Resurrection declares that suffering and death will not have the final word.
entries.prayer: Great and faithful God, meet me within what feels larger than I can carry. Lift my eyes toward Jesus and give me courage for the faithful path before me. Amen.
entries.next_step: How might the greatness of God reshape the way you see your present struggle?
entries.closing: The problem may be great, but it is not the greatest reality in the room.

entries.title: Known by the Name of Jesus
entries.greeting: Welcome. Every human badge eventually fades, but the Name of the Lord endures forever.
entries.consider_this:
We naturally speak about the people, teams, communities, and causes we love. They become part of the story we tell about ourselves. Psalm 135 reminds us that the Lord’s Name alone endures through every generation.

To be known as a follower of Jesus is not an invitation to religious performance or superiority. We do not wear His Name as a badge proving that we are better than others. We bear it as people who have received mercy.

Speaking about Jesus matters, but witness includes the character of our lives. Humility, compassion, integrity, courage, and love can make our words believable. When we fail, honest repentance may honour His Name more than defensiveness.

We need not force every conversation or treat people as projects. The Holy Spirit can give natural opportunities to speak about the Hope within us. Our task is to remain ready, gentle, and truthful.
entries.prayer: Lord Jesus, let my life honour Your enduring Name. Give me humble courage to speak of You and form within me a character that reflects the Grace I proclaim. Amen.
entries.next_step: What might it mean for your life to bear the Name of Jesus with humility?
entries.closing: We bear His Name not as the impressive, but as people who have received Grace.

entries.title: Worship in the Darkness
entries.greeting: Welcome. Worship can remain truthful even when joy feels far away.
entries.consider_this:
Praise comes easily when life feels generous. In seasons of sickness, financial strain, grief, or uncertainty, worship may require courage.

Biblical worship does not demand a cheerful performance. The Psalms include lament, protest, questions, silence, and tears. To worship in darkness is not to say that the darkness is good. It is to confess that God remains worthy and present within it.

Sometimes worship is a song. Sometimes it is the whispered Name of Jesus, a prayer borrowed from Scripture, or the decision to remain open to God when the heart feels numb. These quieter expressions are not lesser forms of faith.

God’s goodness is not proved by comfortable circumstances. It is revealed in His faithful Character and most clearly in Jesus, who entered suffering, carried the Cross, and rose again. Because He lives, darkness is real but never ultimate.
entries.prayer: God of Love and Faithfulness, receive the worship I can offer today. Meet me within joy, sorrow, confidence, or numbness, and keep my heart turned toward Jesus. Amen.
entries.next_step: What honest form could worship take within your present emotional reality?
entries.closing: Worship in the darkness does not deny the night; it looks toward the Light that darkness cannot overcome.

entries.title: Courage for What Must Be Faced
entries.greeting: Welcome. God’s answer is not always the removal of trouble; sometimes it is courage within us.
entries.consider_this:
The psalmist called, and God answered by strengthening him. This is an important picture of prayer. God can change circumstances, but He may also meet us by changing what we are able to carry within them.

Christian courage is not aggression, emotional toughness, or the refusal to ask for help. It is faithful action despite fear. Sometimes courage confronts injustice. Sometimes it sets a boundary, tells the truth, enters recovery, asks forgiveness, receives treatment, or simply continues through a difficult day.

We should not assume that every problem will disappear, nor that Jesus responded to suffering with a casual “bring it on.” In Gethsemane, He expressed anguish honestly and entrusted Himself to the Father. His courage included vulnerability, obedience, and love.

The Holy Spirit does not shame us into bravery. He strengthens us for the faithful response that is possible now, often through the presence and care of others.
entries.prayer: God who hears, give me courage for what must be faced. Keep me from pretending that I am unafraid, and strengthen me to take the faithful path with wisdom, humility, and love. Amen.
entries.next_step: What faithful form of courage is God awakening within you?
entries.closing: Courage is not the absence of fear; it is faithfulness within fear.

entries.title: The Nearness God Gives to the Humble
entries.greeting: Welcome. Humility is not thinking less of ourselves; it is living truthfully before God.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 138 tells us that the Lord is exalted, yet He looks with care upon the humble. Pride resists dependence. Humility receives life, strength, wisdom, and Grace as Gifts.

Missing prayer does not automatically prove that someone believes they can live without God. People may be exhausted, grieving, distracted, depressed, or unsure how to begin. Turning prayer into a threat can hide the welcoming Heart of the Father.

At the same time, our habits can reveal where self-reliance has taken root. Humility allows us to admit our need without shame. We can ask for God’s Help before a crisis and receive support from others without feeling diminished.

Jesus reveals that humility is not weakness. Though Lord of all, He served, listened, wept, washed feet, and entrusted Himself to the Father. The Holy Spirit forms this same posture within us: confident in God, honest about our limits, and available to serve.
entries.prayer: Father, free me from pride and from the shame that makes me hide my need. Teach me the humility of Jesus, and draw me into honest dependence upon Your Grace. Amen.
entries.next_step: Where is God inviting you to acknowledge your need without shame?
entries.closing: Humility opens our hands to receive the Grace we were never meant to live without.

entries.title: When Other People Tell Your Story
entries.greeting: Welcome. God knows the whole truth about us, even when others speak without understanding.
entries.consider_this:
Gossip can wound deeply. A distorted story may travel faster than the truth, and we cannot control every conversation or correct every opinion.

Psalm 138 speaks of God preserving the psalmist in trouble. This does not promise that every rumour will be exposed or that reputational damage will never occur. It assures us that hostility does not place us beyond God’s knowledge or care.

There may be times to respond calmly, seek accountability, document what happened, or ask trusted leaders for help. There are also times when chasing every voice only allows gossip to occupy more of our lives. Wisdom helps us recognise the difference.

We can entrust justice to God without wishing harm upon others. We can examine ourselves honestly, correct what is true, release what is false, and refuse to become the kind of people who spread unverified stories.
entries.prayer: God of Truth, You know me fully. Give me wisdom when others speak unfairly, humility where correction is needed, and peace where I must release what I cannot control. Guard my own words from gossip. Amen.
entries.next_step: What would a truthful and Grace-filled response to gossip look like for you?
entries.closing: You do not have to control every version of your story when God knows the truth.

entries.title: Held within God’s Unfinished Work
entries.greeting: Welcome. God does not abandon the Work of His Hands.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 138 expresses confidence that the Lord will fulfil His Purpose. This Hope does not mean that every event happens exactly as God desires or that every personal ambition carries His guarantee.

We live in a world where human choices, injustice, suffering, and loss are real. Not every wall is a promised Jericho, and not every giant will fall in the way we expect. Faith does not require us to label evil as good simply because God remains sovereign.

God’s Purpose is most securely revealed in Jesus: to reconcile us to Himself, form us in Christlikeness, gather a People of Grace, and finally renew all things. Circumstances may interrupt our plans, but they cannot force God to abandon His redeeming Work.

We are unfinished people held by a faithful God. He can bring wisdom from disappointment, courage from struggle, and compassion from wounds without calling the wounds good.
entries.prayer: Faithful God, thank You for not abandoning the Work of Your Hands. Correct the purposes I have mistaken for Yours, and continue forming the Life of Jesus within me. Amen.
entries.next_step: Where do you need to trust God’s ongoing Work without demanding a particular outcome?
entries.closing: Your plans may change, but God has not abandoned His Work within you.

entries.title: Fully Known, Still Welcomed
entries.greeting: Welcome. God knows our words, thoughts, movements, and motives—and He still invites us near.
entries.consider_this:
Much of life is lived before an audience. We shape appearances, manage impressions, and hope others notice what is admirable. Yet Psalm 139 brings us before the God who sees beneath every image.

Being known this deeply can feel uncomfortable. God sees what others miss, including our hidden fears, mixed motives, and unspoken wounds. But His knowledge is not cold surveillance. It is personal, attentive, and surrounded by His Presence.

Spiritual maturity is not measured by whether we completed a devotional routine before leaving home. Prayer and Scripture are precious Gifts, but exhaustion, caregiving, illness, or emotional struggle can disrupt familiar rhythms. God’s invitation is not into performance but honest relationship.

Because Jesus has opened the way through Grace, we can stop managing an image before God. We can confess, receive mercy, and allow the Holy Spirit to transform the person beneath the surface.
entries.prayer: God who knows me, free me from the pressure to impress You or others. Meet me beneath the image I present, and form integrity, healing, and truth within me. Amen.
entries.next_step: What part of your inner life needs to be welcomed honestly into God’s Presence?
entries.closing: The God who sees beneath the surface is also the God who welcomes you by Grace.

entries.title: Wonderfully Made and Deeply Valued
entries.greeting: Welcome. Your life carries God-given dignity that no opinion, failure, or statistic can erase.
entries.consider_this:
The psalmist praises God for the wonder of being made and for the countless thoughts of God that surround him. Human life is not accidental or disposable. Every person bears dignity as someone created by God.

This truth does not make us invincible, superior, or exempt from struggle. Nor does our value depend upon becoming impressive for the Kingdom. We are people, not machines. God welcomes our limits, our need for rest, and the parts of our story that remain tender.

Remembering our dignity can change what we accept from others and what we believe about ourselves. Being made by God does not require remaining in degrading or abusive circumstances. Wise support and healthy boundaries can honour the life He has entrusted to us.

Our deepest identity is not found in productivity, appearance, popularity, or even ministry success. In Christ, we are loved, called, and invited to become more fully the people God created us to be.
entries.prayer: Creator God, help me receive the dignity You have given me and recognise it in others. Heal the voices that have distorted my identity, and teach me to live as someone deeply valued by You. Amen.
entries.next_step: Which false label needs to lose its authority over the way you see yourself?
entries.closing: You are not a number or a machine; you are a person wonderfully made and deeply valued by God.

entries.title: The Kindness of Wise Correction
entries.greeting: Welcome. A teachable heart can receive correction without losing its dignity.
entries.consider_this:
The psalmist describes correction from a righteous person as kindness. This does not mean every criticism is accurate or every correction is delivered well. Some words are manipulative, shaming, or abusive and should not be accepted as godly authority.

Wise correction is different. It is rooted in truth, offered with humility, and concerned with restoration rather than control. Receiving it can reveal blind spots and open a path toward growth.

Defensiveness often rises because being wrong feels threatening. Grace reminds us that our worth is not built upon always being right. We can listen carefully, test what is said against Scripture, consider the character of the person speaking, and receive whatever is true.

A teachable spirit also changes the way we correct others. We speak gently, acknowledge our own limits, and leave room for conversation. The goal is not to win but to help one another become more faithful.
entries.prayer: God of Wisdom, give me humility to receive what is true and discernment to recognise what is harmful. Teach me to offer correction with the gentleness and Grace of Jesus. Amen.
entries.next_step: How do you usually respond when trustworthy correction touches a tender place?
entries.closing: Grace frees us to learn because being wrong does not make us worthless.

entries.title: Remembering Grace in the Darkness
entries.greeting: Welcome. When trouble narrows our vision, remembering can help us see beyond the present moment.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 143 holds darkness, weakness, and Hope within the same prayer. The psalmist does not hide his distress. He remembers what God has done and asks to hear of His unfailing Love.

Problems can consume attention and make the future feel closed. Remembering past Grace may restore perspective, but it should not become pressure to feel better immediately. Depression, trauma, and anxiety can affect memory and concentration. Faithful care may include pastoral support, counselling, medical help, rest, and safe companionship.

God’s past faithfulness does not mean He will repeat the same outcome. What He did before may not happen in the same way again. The unchanging truth is His Character: He remains present, compassionate, wise, and able to sustain us.

Sometimes remembering reveals dramatic deliverance. Sometimes it reveals enough Grace for a difficult day. Both can become testimony.
entries.prayer: Faithful God, meet me where darkness has narrowed my vision. Help me remember Your Grace without denying my present pain, and lead me toward the care and Hope I need. Amen.
entries.next_step: Which memory of God’s Grace can sit gently beside what you are facing now?
entries.closing: Remembering does not erase today’s pain; it reminds us that pain is not the only truth.

entries.title: Faith That Travels Beyond Us
entries.greeting: Welcome. God’s greatness becomes a story received, lived, and shared across generations.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 145 pictures one generation commending God’s Works to another. Faith is personal, but it was never meant to end with us.

Sharing faith does not require knowing everything or becoming an expert teacher. None of us carries another person’s eternal destiny. Salvation belongs to God, and the Holy Spirit works in ways we cannot control.

We can still grow in our understanding so that we speak about Jesus clearly and faithfully. We learn Scripture, ask questions, listen to mature believers, and allow our lives to be shaped by the truth we hope to share.

Discipleship often happens through ordinary relationships: a conversation, a prayer, an apology, a story of Grace, or patient presence over time. Children and new believers need more than information. They need to see what repentance, forgiveness, worship, service, and Hope look like within real life.
entries.prayer: Great and gracious God, deepen my understanding of Your Word and make my life a trustworthy witness. Give me humility and courage to share what I have received with those who come after me. Amen.
entries.next_step: What part of God’s faithfulness would you most want another generation to know?
entries.closing: We pass on faith not as experts with every answer, but as witnesses to the Grace we have received.

entries.title: Formed by Grace and Compassion
entries.greeting: Welcome. The Lord is gracious, compassionate, patient, and rich in Love.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 145 does more than describe God. It reveals the Character the Holy Spirit forms within those who walk with Him.

Anger itself is not always sinful. It can alert us to injustice, violation, exhaustion, or grief. The question is what anger produces and whether it remains beneath the Lordship of Jesus.

Being slow to anger does not mean suppressing every concern, overlooking abuse, or remaining silent when truth must be spoken. Grace can be both gentle and courageous. Compassion seeks to understand, while wisdom establishes boundaries where harm continues.

It would be unfair to treat irritability or emotional struggle as proof that someone does not spend time with God. Stress, trauma, illness, and mental health can affect how people respond. Spiritual formation includes prayer and Scripture, but may also involve rest, counselling, treatment, apology, and learning healthier ways to communicate.

God meets us patiently as He reshapes our reactions. His kindness becomes the place from which change grows.
entries.prayer: Gracious God, let Your Compassion shape my words and responses. Help me understand what lies beneath my anger, speak truth without cruelty, and receive the help I need to grow. Amen.
entries.next_step: What might your anger be revealing that needs God’s Wisdom and compassionate care?
entries.closing: God’s patience does not shame us; it creates room for us to become more like Jesus.

entries.title: Jesus Is Not a Means to an End
entries.greeting: Welcome. The greatest Gift of the Christian life is not what Jesus gives us, but Jesus Himself.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 145 celebrates the Lord as righteous, loving, near, and attentive to those who call upon Him. These Gifts arise from relationship with God rather than a transaction designed to obtain the life we want.

We can begin to treat prayer as a way to secure outcomes, Scripture as a formula for success, or obedience as leverage for blessing. Jesus refuses to become a means to an end. He is Lord, Saviour, and the Centre toward which every part of life is drawn.

Loving Jesus above family, work, study, or ambition does not mean neglecting those responsibilities. It means receiving them beneath His Lordship. Love for Him should make us more faithful, compassionate, honest, and present within the relationships He has entrusted to us.

Apart from Jesus, we cannot reconcile ourselves to God. Yet those who belong to Him are not nothing. They are beloved people made in God’s Image, redeemed by Grace, and invited to bear fruit through the Holy Spirit.
entries.prayer: Lord Jesus, forgive me for seeking Your Gifts while neglecting Your Presence. Be the Centre of my life, and teach me to receive every other responsibility beneath Your loving Lordship. Amen.
entries.next_step: Where might you be seeking something from Jesus while overlooking relationship with Him?
entries.closing: Jesus does not merely give us a better life; He gives us Himself.

entries.title: The God Who Draws Near to the Vulnerable
entries.greeting: Welcome. God’s Heart turns toward people who are oppressed, hungry, displaced, and alone.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 146 describes a God who upholds the oppressed, feeds the hungry, gives freedom, lifts the bowed down, and watches over those who are vulnerable.

The Church is called to reflect this Compassion. We do not serve to prove ourselves, rescue people as though they have no agency, or reduce them to projects. We draw near because every person bears God’s Image and deserves dignity, attention, and love.

Compassion may involve practical help, generous giving, advocacy, listening, safeguarding, hospitality, professional service, or standing against systems that cause harm. No individual can meet every need. The Body of Christ serves together, discerning what faithfulness looks like within the gifts and limits God has given.

We should resist both indifference and condemning pressure. The Holy Spirit awakens willing participation, not frantic guilt. Jesus moves us beyond convenience while also teaching us to serve sustainably, wisely, and with others.
entries.prayer: God of Compassion, open my eyes to people whose pain is easily overlooked. Free me from indifference and from unhealthy guilt. Show me how to serve with dignity, wisdom, courage, and love. Amen.
entries.next_step: Whose experience might God be inviting you to notice with greater compassion?
entries.closing: When God’s Compassion shapes us, vulnerable people become neighbours rather than interruptions.

entries.title: Let Everything That Breathes Praise the Lord
entries.greeting: Welcome to the final day of this journey through the Psalms. We end where every faithful journey leads: in praise.
entries.consider_this:
Psalm 150 gathers everything that breathes into worship. Praise is not reserved for days when health, finances, relationships, and emotions align. It rises because God is worthy.

This does not mean forcing celebration when the heart is grieving. The Psalms have taught us that lament, silence, questions, and tears can all belong within faithful worship. Praise does not erase the truth of the year behind us. It places every joy, wound, failure, and sign of Grace before God.

As this devotional journey closes, we remember that Scripture was never meant merely to fill a year. God’s Word invites a lifelong walk with Jesus. The same Lord who met us in these Psalms continues to lead through His Word, His Spirit, and His People.

We praise because Jesus has reconciled us to God through the Cross, risen from the dead, and given us a Hope that reaches beyond every ending.
entries.prayer: Lord Jesus, receive the year I bring before You. Thank You for every place Your Grace has met me. Keep me walking within Your Word, Your Presence, and the fellowship of Your People. Let my life become praise. Amen.
entries.next_step: As this journey closes, what truth from the Psalms do you want to carry forward with Jesus?
entries.closing: The devotional ends, but the walk continues: let everything that breathes praise the Lord.
